questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between Merge and Append?
options: Merge combines sideways by adding columns via a shared key; Append combines downward by stacking rows
They are two names for the exact same operation
Merge only works with numbers; Append only works with text
Append requires a shared key column, and Merge does not
questions.explain: Merge reaches sideways — joining on a shared key to add columns from another table. Append reaches downward — stacking rows from tables that already share the same columns.

questions.q: Merge is most similar to which familiar Excel tool?
options: VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP, but pulling back a whole matched row's worth of columns instead of one value
AutoSum
Conditional Formatting
The Name Box
questions.explain: Like VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, Merge finds matching rows based on a shared key — the difference is Merge brings back an entire set of matched columns at once, not just a single looked-up value.

questions.q: What does Append assume about the tables you're combining?
options: That they already share the same (or similar) columns, just different rows
That they share a unique key column to match on
That one table has more columns than the other
Nothing — Append works on any two unrelated tables
questions.explain: Append is built for tables with matching column layouts — like monthly sales files — and simply stacks their rows into one combined table.

questions.q: What happens if you Append two tables whose column names don't match exactly?
options: Append still runs, but creates a separate column for each name variant instead of combining them
Append fails immediately with an error
Power Query automatically renames the columns to match
The mismatched columns are silently deleted
questions.explain: Append doesn't reconcile differently-named columns for you — mismatched names end up as separate columns, which is why renaming columns to match before appending is the safer order of operations.

questions.q: You have two tables that share a ProductID column but otherwise have completely different columns, and you want to enrich one table with fields from the other. Which command do you use?
options: Merge
Append
Remove Duplicates
Split Column by Delimiter
questions.explain: A shared key column plus a need to bring in different columns from another table is exactly the Merge scenario — Append would be the wrong tool since these tables don't share the same columns to stack.
